exemplars.title: Talk to the Hand: an LLM-powered Chatbot with Visual Pointer as Proactive Companion for On-Screen Tasks
exemplars.why: The agent is rendered as a second mouse cursor inside the active screen surface, with communication attached directly to that cursor and no dedicated chat-log area. This is an unusually complete match for the pattern: the agent has a persistent, pointer-relative visible form in the user's coordinate space, and its location identifies where assistance is focused.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over Fairy Cursor because the evidence establishes not only a pointer-following embodiment but also attached communication and the explicit removal of a separate agent container.

exemplars.title: Exploring Fairy Cursor as a Form of AI Agent for In-the-Flow Assistance: Design Opportunities and Challenges
exemplars.why: Fairy Cursor turns the assistive agent into a lightweight visual companion that follows the mouse pointer, keeping its presence attached to the user's locus of action. The pointer anchoring is a direct, portable implementation of in-situ presence and makes the agent part of the work surface rather than a detached conversational destination.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over CreepyCoCreator because its pointer-attached presence is a more literal match for the structural signature and transfers more readily across ordinary on-screen workflows.

exemplars.title: CreepyCoCreator? Investigating AI Representation Modes for 3D Object Co-Creation in Virtual Reality
exemplars.why: The AI incrementally adds and modifies highlighted elements at selected positions within the shared 3D artifact while the user continues painting. Its actions are spatially anchored, visibly attributable, and interleaved with the user's work, demonstrating the pattern through live artifact manipulation rather than a pointer companion.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over PointAloud because it shows the AI visibly touching and changing the shared artifact, whereas PointAloud's evidence establishes pointer-adjacent capture feedback but not a comparably clear agent presence or direct artifact intervention.

notes: The final ranking follows the consensus top three; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The first two exemplars are intentionally close variants because both provide exceptionally direct evidence for the pattern's attached-companion branch, while the third adds a distinct shared-artifact manifestation. Evidence should still be treated cautiously: none of the supplied quotations demonstrates measured outcome impact; Fairy Cursor's excerpt establishes its following form but not its concrete assistance or state transitions; and CreepyCoCreator relies on a truncated figure caption and a VR-specific implementation. The disagreement around CreepyCoCreator chiefly concerns generalizability, not whether its highlighted, position-specific interventions satisfy the structural signature.
